quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #17
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: You should leave extra space in front of your vehicle when following a:

options.text: Station wagon.
Passenger vehicle.
Motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Leave extra space behind a motorcycle. Motorcycles can stop faster than other vehicles. You need room to stop if the motorcycle brakes suddenly or the rider falls. Motorcycles are also harder to see at night because they have only one tail light.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Trucks entering.
Truck exit only.
Steep downgrade ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steep downgrade ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a steep downhill section is coming. Check your brakes.

questions.question: If your vehicle breaks down on a public road and you need to stop, you should:

options.text: Stop where you are and turn on your hazard lights.
Stop where you are and hold down your horn.
Pull off the right side of the road and turn on your hazard lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull off the right side of the road and turn on your hazard lights.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle breaks down, pull off the right side of the road if you can. Turn on your hazard lights so other drivers can see you and know you need help.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Cars in the right lane must slow down.
No left turn.
Merge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign tells you that traffic may merge from the right. Be ready to let traffic merge safely.

questions.question: A large truck ahead of you is turning right onto a street with two lanes in each direction. The truck:

options.text: May complete its turn in either of the two lanes.
May have to swing wide to complete the right turn.
Must stay in the right lane at all times while turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: May have to swing wide to complete the right turn.
questions.explanation: When turning, the rear wheels follow a shorter path than the front wheels. Long trucks need extra space to turn. They often must swing wide to complete a right turn without hitting things.

questions.question: If your vehicle has a mechanical problem:

options.text: Signal and pull into the slow lane.
Stop in your lane and put on your hazard lights.
Put on your hazard lights and pull off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put on your hazard lights and pull off the road.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle breaks down on a highway, turn on your emergency flashers. Get your vehicle off the road and away from traffic so other drivers can see you safely.

questions.question: Work zone barriers, drums, cones, and signs are used to:

options.text: Make drivers angry about slow traffic.
Inconvenience drivers.
Keep traffic out of hazardous work zones.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep traffic out of hazardous work zones.
questions.explanation: Work zones are dangerous for workers and drivers. Watch for cones, barrels, signs, large vehicles, and workers in bright vests. They warn you and show you how to drive safely through the work zone.

questions.question: Before you back up your vehicle, you should:

options.text: Check behind the vehicle before getting in.
Depend entirely on your mirrors.
Accelerate quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check behind the vehicle before getting in.
questions.explanation: Before backing up, check behind your vehicle. Children and small objects are hard to see from the driver's seat.

questions.question: You are on the freeway and traffic is merging into your lane. You should:

options.text: Make room for the merging traffic, if possible.
Assert your right-of-way by driving faster.
Always maintain your position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make room for the merging traffic, if possible.
questions.explanation: When you can, make room to let vehicles merge safely into your lane.

questions.question: On a green arrow, you must:

options.text: Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian in the intersection.
Yield to pedestrians only in the intersection.
Wait four seconds before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means "go." Turn in the direction the arrow points. First, yield to any vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians still in the intersection.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line between two lanes mean?

options.text: Both lanes go in the same direction.
You can pass when it is safe.
You cannot pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line separates lanes going in opposite directions. You can pass if there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What does this sign warn you about?

options.text: A railroad crossing ahead.
A pedestrian crossing ahead.
A no passing zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: A railroad crossing ahead.
questions.explanation: Round signs with yellow and black markings warn drivers about railroad crossings. This is the only use for round warning signs.

questions.question: When must drivers yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk?

options.text: Only if the pedestrians wave first.
Only if the pedestrians are not texting.
Always.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always.
questions.explanation: Always stop at a crosswalk to let pedestrians cross. Only move forward when your lane is completely clear.

questions.question: What is the biggest risk when you are fatigued while driving?

options.text: Missing an exit.
Being late for an appointment.
Falling asleep and crashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Falling asleep and crashing.
questions.explanation: Fatigue makes it hard to judge speed and distance. You could fall asleep behind the wheel and crash, hurting or killing yourself or others.

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Stop before entering the intersection.
Slow down and look both ways, then proceed carefully.
Wait for a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and look both ways, then proceed carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down, check for traffic crossing your path, and go with caution.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in a construction zone?

options.text: Speed up slightly.
Be prepared for anything unusual.
Expect construction workers to get out of your way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be prepared for anything unusual.
questions.explanation: Construction zones have unexpected hazards. Drive very carefully for your safety and the safety of workers and other drivers.

questions.question: Which is a safe driving technique?

options.text: Using high beam lights in fog.
Staring straight ahead at the road.
Checking your mirrors often.

questions.correctAnswerText: Checking your mirrors often.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors every two to five seconds to see hazards around you. Do not stare only ahead. In fog, use low beam lights, not high beams.

questions.question: When can you cross double yellow lines to pass?

options.text: When the car in front moves right to let you pass.
When the yellow line on your side is broken.
When the yellow line on the other side is broken.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the yellow line on your side is broken.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line on your side means you can pass if it is safe. A solid yellow line on your side means you cannot pass.

questions.question: When passing a motorcycle, you must:

options.text: Stay in the right lane because the motorcycle does not use the whole lane.
Honk your horn to make the motorcycle move to the shoulder.
Be completely in the left lane before, during, and after the pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be completely in the left lane before, during, and after the pass.
questions.explanation: Give the motorcycle a full lane when passing. Do not share a lane with a motorcycle. Returning to the right lane too soon can force the rider off the road.

questions.question: When is a highway most slippery?

options.text: After it has been raining for several hours.
When rain first starts.
After it has been raining for one to two hours.

questions.correctAnswerText: When rain first starts.
questions.explanation: When rain first starts, dirt and oil on the road mix with water. This creates a slippery coating.

questions.question: To see objects in your blind spot when changing lanes, you should check:

options.text: Only the left outside mirror.
Over your left or right shoulder.
Only the inside rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over your left or right shoulder.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Look over the correct shoulder to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Hospital.
Upcoming intersection.
Railroad crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Upcoming intersection.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. This sign tells drivers an intersection is coming up so they can prepare to turn or watch for other traffic.

questions.question: If pedestrians are crossing illegally in the middle of the street instead of at a crosswalk, you:

options.text: Must stop for them.
Do not have to stop for them.
Should honk your horn at them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must stop for them.
questions.explanation: You must always stop for pedestrians. Even if they are crossing where they should not be, you must still stop for them.

questions.question: When a driver behind you wants to pass, you should:

options.text: Speed up.
Slow down by easing off the accelerator to help them pass.
Brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down by easing off the accelerator to help them pass.
questions.explanation: When a driver is passing you, ease off the accelerator to help them pass safely. You may need to slow down so they can return to your lane.

questions.question: You can help keep the driver behind you at a safe distance by:

options.text: Driving 10 mph faster than the car behind you.
Driving 10 mph slower than the car behind you.
Driving at a steady speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving at a steady speed.
questions.explanation: Drive at a steady speed to help the driver behind you maintain a safe distance. Also signal your turns, lane changes, and slowdowns in advance.

questions.question: You are in an intersection and an emergency vehicle approaches with its siren and flashing lights. You should:

options.text: Stop immediately in the intersection.
Pull to the right and stop before entering the intersection.
Finish crossing the intersection, then pull right and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Finish crossing the intersection, then pull right and stop.
questions.explanation: If you are already in an intersection when an emergency vehicle approaches with flashing lights or a siren, continue through and then drive to the right and stop. You must always give emergency vehicles the right-of-way.

questions.question: When should you use your horn?

options.text: To greet another driver.
Whenever it may help prevent a crash.
When you are angry with another driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Whenever it may help prevent a crash.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to get a driver's attention if there is danger ahead. Sound your horn whenever it can help prevent a crash.

questions.question: This sign shows that the road ahead:

options.text: Turns sharply right, then left.
Curves right, then left.
Curves right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Curves right, then left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road curves to the right, then curves to the left.

questions.question: Tailgating (driving too close to another car's rear bumper):

options.text: Can make other drivers angry and frustrated.
Never results in a traffic ticket.
Prevents other drivers from cutting you off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can make other drivers angry and frustrated.
questions.explanation: Tailgating is dangerous behavior that can lead to aggressive driving and legal trouble. Avoid tailgating other drivers.

questions.question: Hydroplaning happens when tires slide on water instead of gripping the road. To prevent hydroplaning in wet weather, you should:

options.text: Use cruise control to keep a constant speed.
Slow down.
Move to the shoulder as soon as it rains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast on wet roads. Slow down when driving on wet pavement to prevent hydroplaning.

questions.question: When you see a flashing yellow light at an intersection, you must:

options.text: Stop completely at the intersection.
Keep driving at your normal speed.
Slow down and drive carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and drive carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light tells you to be alert. Slow down and proceed with care.

questions.question: A vehicle suddenly cuts in front of you. What should you do first?

options.text: Honk and brake hard.
Release the gas pedal.
Swerve into the next lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: Releasing the gas pedal creates space between you and the other vehicle. You avoid hard braking or swerving.

questions.question: A traffic light is green, but a police officer signals you to stop. You should:

options.text: Obey the officer.
Obey the traffic light.
Do what the car ahead does.

questions.correctAnswerText: Obey the officer.
questions.explanation: Always obey a police officer's directions, even if they conflict with traffic signals or signs.

questions.question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaching, you must:

options.text: Keep your speed and stay in your lane until it passes.
Move to the right lane and drive slowly until it passes.
Pull to the edge of the road and stop until it passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the edge of the road and stop until it passes.
questions.explanation: Pull over to the right edge of the road and stop. On one-way streets, move to the nearest edge.

questions.question: When turning left at an intersection:

options.text: You must always let oncoming traffic and pedestrians go first.
Oncoming traffic and pedestrians must let you go first.
You never have to let oncoming traffic and pedestrians go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must always let oncoming traffic and pedestrians go first.
questions.explanation: Always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians when turning left. Make your turn only when the intersection is clear.

questions.question: You are parking downhill on a two-way road with no curb. Which way should you turn your wheels?

options.text: Straight ahead
Right, toward the side of the road
Left, toward the center of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Right, toward the side of the road
questions.explanation: When parking downhill, turn your wheels toward the road edge. This way, if your brakes fail, the car rolls away from traffic, not into it. When parking uphill with a curb, turn wheels toward the center so the car rolls into the curb.

questions.question: Bad suspension can cause:

options.text: Problems controlling your vehicle.
Squealing brakes.
Loose steering.

questions.correctAnswerText: Problems controlling your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Suspension helps you control your vehicle and provides a smooth ride. If your car bounces a lot after bumps or is hard to control, you may need new suspension parts.

questions.question: You are following a large truck on the freeway. You should drive:

options.text: Close behind the truck in bad weather because the driver can see ahead better.
Farther back than you would from a regular car.
Just one car length back so the driver can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther back than you would from a regular car.
questions.explanation: If you drive too close to a truck, the truck driver cannot see you. Staying far back gives you more time to stop if the truck brakes suddenly.

questions.question: On a slippery road, your following distance should be:

options.text: The same as normal.
Farther than normal.
Closer than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther than normal.
questions.explanation: On slippery roads, your car needs more distance to stop. Keep a longer distance between your car and the one ahead.

questions.question: This speed limit sign means:

options.text: You must drive through the intersection at this speed.
The highest safe speed under good conditions is 55 mph.
You cannot drive slower than this speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: The highest safe speed under good conditions is 55 mph.
questions.explanation: This sign shows the maximum speed limit for that road. You can drive slower based on conditions, but you cannot drive faster than the posted limit.
